chunks: 9 – Al-Ḥasan b. Asad, al-Ṭafāwī, al-Baṣrī, Abū Muḥammad.

He narrated from weak narrators, and they narrate from him. His madhhab is corrupt. I do not know anything in which he is more sound except for his narration of the book of ʿAlī b. Ismāʿīl b. Shuʿayb b. Mītham, and people other than him have narrated it.
ai.seo_question: Who is Al-Hasan ibn Asad al-Tafawi and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?
ai.summary: This biographical entry from 'Ilm al-Rijāl describes Al-asan ibn Asad al-Tafawi as a narrator who transmits from weak narrators and is considered to have a corrupt creed (madhhab). The author notes that his primary merit lies in his narration of the book of Ali ibn Isma'il, a work also transmitted by others.
